body: Follow-up from #676 (its red-team asked for an addressee): #676 stamps the `scan-build-18` row with the clang that scan-build's own lookup would pick. That lookup is `$RealBin/bin/clang`, then `$RealBin/clang`, then the Debian/Ubuntu default `/usr/lib/llvm-18/bin/clang` (`_SCAN_BUILD_DISTRO_CLANG` in `static_analysis_diff.py`). The distro-patched `FindClang` default was measured only on `clang-tools-15` (Ubuntu 22.04's newest). Whoever takes this issue onto an LLVM-18 host should also re-measure the scan-build-18 wrapper's default analyzer path, and confirm that the stamp names the clang that actually runs.

Cross-reference: #696 (a failed static row stops step 13, a breaking change) lands after this issue and treats the new `error: scan-build-18 not analyzed` route as one that stops step 13. If this issue lands after #696 instead, it needs its own release ruling, because adding an error route to a row that decides step 13 would then change step 13's outcome.

**Operator ruling on the OPEN QUESTION (2026-10-08): option (2), whole-build.**

Once scan-build-18 actually analyzes, its row keeps today's whole-build shape (`- | - | pass/FAIL`). All checkers stay enabled, with no `-disable-checker` and no baseline. Under this answer:
- The deduplication AC and test (a‴) do not apply, since both are scoped "under (1)".
- The module docstring, commands/analyze.md and the CHANGELOG state that the row is a deliberate exception to spec §18's "all paths are diff-scoped".

Effect on volk: the row will read `FAIL: 18 bug(s) found` until those findings are fixed. Per #696, findings never decide step 13, so this is report-only. The 18 are all `deadcode.DeadStores` (dead initializations, assignments and increments). The operator chose to fix them at the source rather than suppress the checker; that work is tracked in mtibbits/volk#249. The 18 were measured on a fork work branch, not on volk main, so #249's first step re-measures them on main.

The mechanism (a dedicated dir configured under scan-build, or analyze-build-18 over a built compile database) is left to the implementation plan.
